purpose: Every number printed in the documents listed under `scope` resolves here to the raw result file, the exact command, the dataset, the sample size and the caveats that belong with it. A claim with no entry is a claim with no evidence. Task B2 renders the documents from this file so the two cannot drift.

excludes: fenced code blocks - shell commands and illustrative terminal output, not measurements

longmemeval_oracle.name: LongMemEval-oracle
longmemeval_oracle.citation: Wu et al., LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory, ICLR 2025
longmemeval_oracle.sha256_note: The dataset is third-party and not committed (see research/data/README.md). No hash was recorded when the results were produced, so the exact revision used cannot be proven. Recording it is a prerequisite for task F7.
longmemeval_oracle.ground_truth: human-annotated answer_session_ids - independent of this project's embeddings

longmemeval_oracle_sample40.name: LongMemEval-oracle, 40-question sample
longmemeval_oracle_sample40.sampling_note: The sample is not seeded in the recorded run; the selection cannot be reproduced exactly.

live_validation_tasks.name: 12 hand-written coding micro-tasks
live_validation_tasks.note: Four project-specific invented-API tasks plus eight generic pitfalls; the check is regex/AST, never execution.

poisoning_corpus.name: hand-written poisoning taxonomy
poisoning_corpus.note: 12 attacks and 10 benign notes. A proof of taxonomy, not a benchmark - see research/POISONING.md.

owner_vault_snapshot.name: the owner's private bilingual vault
owner_vault_snapshot.note: ~320 notes across 11 projects. Private, so no third party can reproduce any number derived from it. Every such claim is marked with a raw_gap.

demo_store.name: throwaway store built by examples/scenario_demo.py
demo_store.note: Deterministic capture with fixed exit codes is task C1.

local_bge_m3.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 7700, 32 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB)

local_bge_m3_competitors.embedder: bge-m3 via local Ollama - identical for every system
local_bge_m3_competitors.note: Mem0, LangMem and A-MEM run from their own packages on the same stand and the same embedder, so the comparison isolates the ranker, not the embedder.
local_bge_m3_competitors.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 7700, 32 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB)

qwen25_3b_reader.note: A deliberately weak reader; the accuracy dip is reported, not hidden.

ryzen7700_win11_py314.note: End-to-end subprocess timing: stdin event to process exit, no model and no network.

stdlib_only.note: Standard library only - no model, no network, no GPU.

demo_no_embedder.note: No embedder reachable, so recall falls back to lexical search. This is what a fresh clone and CI get, and what `NEVERTWICE_EMBED_PROVIDER=none` pins.

demo_local_embedder.note: An Ollama server running locally with bge-m3 pulled. The demo takes the semantic path here and reports a different ratio than the same command does without one.

non_metrics.reason: single digit - table headers (R@1, R@3, R@5), k values, list markers and the literal zeros in '0 dependencies' and '0 tokens until they fire'. Too ambiguous to bind to a claim; task B2 generates these positions instead of matching them.
a year - dates such as 2026-07, not a measurement
a Python version in the support matrix
percent-encoded fragment of the LongMemEval badge label ('%20›%200.76')
the month fragment of an ISO date such as 2026-07
the k in the 'R@10' and 'k=10' table positions
percent-encoding fragments inside a badge URL; the badge's human-readable claim is covered by its own claim entry
the count of headline claims, baselines and pairs, tallied by the renderer from this manifest rather than measured
a verdict tally in the generated baseline summary, counted by the renderer from this manifest

drift_note: A drift entry records a number a document prints that the stored raw result contradicts. All five entries opened by task B1 were closed by task B2: the tables are generated from this manifest now, and the prose around them was corrected to the stored values. Open a new entry when a published figure is found to disagree and cannot be corrected in the same change; the test fails once the document no longer prints it, so an entry cannot outlive its fix.

baseline_policy.rule: A headline is publishable only when it clears every applicable baseline below under matched conditions. A baseline that was not run is recorded as `not_compared`, never omitted: an unrun baseline is the most likely explanation a reader will reach for.
matched_conditions: equal reader model - the same LLM answers in both arms
equal context-token budget - neither arm is allowed more room
equal latency tier - a baseline is not handicapped by being run slower
matched false-positive rate - an intervention that fires more often is not better, it is louder; compare at the same FP rate or report the full curve

verdicts.beats: measured, under matched conditions, and the claim wins
verdicts.ties: measured and within the interval of the baseline
verdicts.loses_to: measured and the baseline wins - the claim must be narrowed or dropped
verdicts.not_compared: not measured yet; the claim is provisional against this baseline
verdicts.not_applicable: the baseline cannot be constructed for this metric; a reason is required

baseline_policy.evidence_rule: A measured verdict (beats / ties / loses_to) must name where the comparison lives: a raw result file, or the claim ids of the two arms. A verdict without evidence is an assertion, and flipping `not_compared` to `beats` must therefore cost something.

no_memory.name: no memory
no_memory.definition: the same agent, same task, with the memory system switched off
no_memory.why: the floor. Any memory that cannot beat its own absence is overhead.
no_memory.how: run the harness with the memory arm disabled

full_history.name: full-history injection
full_history.definition: paste the entire accumulated history into the context instead of retrieving
full_history.why: the dumb baseline that often wins when the history is small; it is what a user does by hand before installing anything.
full_history.how: python research/token_ab.py (the `net vs the full history` column)

lexical_recall.name: lexical recall (BM25)
lexical_recall.definition: term-overlap retrieval with no embedder and no model
lexical_recall.why: zero-dependency, zero-latency, and repeatedly close to far more complicated systems. LoCoMo was discredited partly because BM25 nearly won it.

curated_agents_md.name: a curated AGENTS.md
curated_agents_md.definition: one hand-written instructions file that a person maintains
curated_agents_md.why: the honest competitor for most of what agent memory claims. If a human writing five lines gets the same prevention, the machinery is not earning its place.

llm_session_summary.name: an LLM session summary
llm_session_summary.definition: ask the model to summarise the session and inject that summary next time
llm_session_summary.why: the cheapest possible 'memory', available in one prompt with no system at all
llm_session_summary.how: python research/cheap_baselines.py - **arm built, run GATED**: it runs against a deterministic extractive summariser, never against a model, and is reported as `session_summary_extractive`

linter_or_test.name: the relevant linter or test
linter_or_test.definition: the existing static check that already catches the same class of mistake
linter_or_test.why: several guard-shaped pitfalls (f-string SQL, bare except, missing close) are caught by ruff, bandit or a unit test. A guard that duplicates a linter is not memory, it is a worse linter.
linter_or_test.how: python research/cheap_baselines.py (the `linter_or_test` row) - **built, F2**, as an oracle upper bound on static analysis

curated_haystack.name: an already-curated small haystack
curated_haystack.definition: the handful of sessions that actually contain the answer, pasted whole
curated_haystack.why: stricter than full-history injection at small scale, and this project already runs it. Recording only the six the policy names would hide the harder test.
curated_haystack.how: python research/token_ab.py (the `net vs a curated small haystack` column)

withdrawal.what_happened: Every claim in this manifest carried commit 05cfdc96 - the commit that last *touched the artifact file*, which was a directory move, not the commit whose code produced the number. B1/B2 had closed document-to-artifact drift and left artifact-to-code drift wide open, so the published corpus described the v1.0.0 engine after four rounds of review had rewritten the ranker beneath it.
withdrawal.what_was_done: Each claim now carries `produced_by`, the repository files its command imports, and tools/check_freshness.py fails when any of them changed after the claim's commit. Artifacts whose generators run here - CPU, no key, no gated dataset - were regenerated at HEAD and restamped. The rest are withdrawn: kept in this file with a reason, removed from every published document.
withdrawal.how_to_restore: python tools/check_freshness.py --list-stale names each withdrawn number and its gate. Clearing a gate means committing the dataset with a hash, spending the gated API budget, or running on the owner's own store - then re-running the claim's `command` and restamping `commit`.
